main_body: A roofed water stall: a slate-tile roof on two wooden posts, with a stone basin of water between the posts at the bottom.
top_band: At the middle column, rows 1-3 are a light grey cap, then rows 4-15 are lighter slate-blue roof slope with tile columns. Rows 16-17 are a dark eave edge. The basin has a light grey rim at rows 30-31, with its water surface inside it at rows 31-35.
evidence: The roof reads as a large sloped surface seen from above, with a dark eave line and shadow under it, like the reference well roof. The basin shows a rim and an inset water surface (about 5 rows) above a grey front face at rows 36-43. The posts stand open and the back area is set back, so the piece is a 3/4 drawing with real horizontal surfaces and a front face.

style.evidence: The roof has about 5 steps with tile columns and per-tile highlights, which is close to the reference. The basin front is a large flat grey block of about 14x8 px with almost no grain, and the water is a flat blue fill with one highlight bar. The posts are flat orange-brown strips with only 2-3 tones. The outline is a dark navy that is close to near-black in places rather than a consistent dark tone of the neighbouring material. Overall the lower half is thinner and flatter than the reference stall and well.
